corrected_value.title: Changes in fat distribution (WHR) and body weight across the menstrual cycle.

decisions.location: The Current Study (lines 185-188); see also Results (lines 569-574), Discussion (lines 629-632), and References (lines 1091-1093)
decisions.quote:
The  objective  of  the  current  research  was  to  provide  an  operational  replication  of 
the finding that women’s faces are more attractive at high fertility (Roberts et al., 2004) and 
of  the  finding  that  women’s  WHRs  are  lower  at  high  fertility  (Kirchengast  and  Gartner, 
2002).
decisions.reason: All three criteria for a genuine missing target are met: (1) the paper explicitly conducts an operational replication of Kirchengast and Gartner's (2002) finding that women's waist-to-hip ratios (WHRs) are lower at high fertility, collecting new waist and hip measurements across high- and low-fertility cycle phases and testing the cycle-phase comparison in Results (lines 541-588, concluding 'Thus, we did not observe the same pattern reported in Kirchengast and Gartner (2002)'); (2) the reference list (lines 1091-1093) establishes the exact bibliographic identity: Kirchengast, S., and Gartner, M. (2002), 'Changes in fat distribution (WHR) and body weight across the menstrual cycle.', Collegium Anthropologicum, 26 (Suppl), 47-57 (no DOI printed); and (3) the sole shipped row (input_row_index '2437', doi_o '10.1098/rsbl.2004.0174') represents only Roberts et al. (2004) on facial attractiveness (sibling blind target_index 1), which is an independent work by different authors in Proceedings of the Royal Society of London B. Prior adjudication and state files (728e7bfe...json and 1d999eaf...json) are absent for this never-adjudicated work.
